item.title: Corporate Transformation in a Changing Landscape: Integrating Technology, Institutions, and Governance
item.content:encoded:
Yanmin He, Otemon Gakuin University

Xikai Chen, California State University

Dongyang Zhang, Capital University of Economics and Business

This special issue addresses how digital technologies, institutional environments, and governance mechanisms interact to shape firm behavior and market evolution. Contemporary firms face complex transformations driven by digitalization and artificial intelligence alongside institutional frictions such as regulatory uncertainty and financing constraints. The special issue seeks to integrate fragmented research streams on digital transformation, corporate governance, and institutional dynamics to develop a more comprehensive understanding of firm-level adaptation in emerging markets.

The call welcomes submissions exploring how digital governance frameworks, enterprise transformation, and corporate governance mechanisms jointly influence innovation and firm competitiveness. Research may examine topics including digital transformation strategies, artificial intelligence adoption, corporate governance structures, institutional frictions affecting finance and trade, geopolitical impacts, and new measurement approaches. Submissions should make significant theoretical or empirical contributions to understanding emerging market dynamics.

  • Corporate governance and strategic adaptation in emerging markets
  • Corporate governance, finance, and trade under institutional frictions
  • Institutional frictions, digital finance, and firms' access to capital
  • Geopolitical uncertainty and firms' strategic reconfiguration
  • New trends in innovation, productivity, and value creation
  • ESG, sustainability, and responsible governance
  • Cross-country differences in technology institutions, and governance
  • Alternative data and new measurement approaches

item.title: Digitalization-Greenization Synergy in Emerging Markets
item.content:encoded:
Haijie Wang, Zhengzhou University

Yanchao Feng, Zhengzhou University

Emerging markets are experiencing structural transformation through the integration of digital technologies with green energy systems, creating opportunities for economic growth and sustainability. This digitalization-greenization synergy aims to enhance efficiency and resilience, yet emerging markets face significant obstacles including regulatory gaps, financial limitations, and unequal access to digital and energy infrastructure.

The special issue seeks research on how this digital-green transition influences macroeconomic dynamics, financial systems, investment patterns, and trade in emerging economies. Theoretical and empirical studies examining inclusive growth, green finance, trade competitiveness, and policy design are particularly welcome, with focus on the economic and financial dimensions of this dual transformation.

item.title: Emerging Market Issues in Asia-Pacific Region
item.content:encoded:
Susan Sunila Sharma, Deakin University

Badri Narayan Rath, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

Alok Kumar Mishra, University of Hyderabad

This special issue examines how geopolitical tensions, particularly conflicts in West Asia, influence international trade dynamics and economic development across the Asia-Pacific region. The initiative brings together academics, researchers, policymakers, and financial experts to explore the interconnections between geopolitical disruptions and trade relationships, and their implications for regional economic stability.

Papers should investigate how recent policy shifts in external, fiscal, and monetary domains reshape trade patterns and economic performance in Asia-Pacific economies. The special issue seeks high-quality research that deepens understanding of these complex relationships and their potential risks to sustainable growth in the region.

Appel publié par Emerging Markets Finance and Trade. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Effects of geopolitical tensions on trade disruption and economic growth in Asia-Pacific Region

  • Complex interconnections between geopolitical tensions and international trade
  • Risks to economic growth stability in the Asia-Pacific Region

item.title: Energy Security and Economic Dynamics in Emerging Markets amid Geopolitical Risk
item.content:encoded:
Susan Sharma, Deakin University

Zhenhua Zhang, Lanzhou University

Jinjun Xue, Nagoya University

Geopolitical tensions are causing significant disruptions in global energy markets, fundamentally affecting energy security and economic stability in emerging markets. These shocks create complex challenges including energy accessibility issues, imported inflation, trade imbalances, and capital flow disruptions that threaten macroeconomic stability and development trajectories.

This special issue seeks to understand how energy security and economic dynamics interact within emerging markets facing geopolitical pressures. The focus is on examining transmission channels between energy sector shocks and broader economic effects, as well as policy responses that emerging economies are implementing through energy diversification, financial hedging, supply chain resilience, and green energy transitions.

The special issue welcomes theoretical and empirical research exploring the interconnections between energy security and economic dynamics, with emphasis on implications for macroeconomic stability, financial resilience, industrial restructuring, sustainable growth, and socioeconomic development in emerging markets.

item.title: Powering Household Portfolio: Digital Finance, Demographics, and Decisions
item.content:encoded:
Weixing Wu, Capital University of Economics and Business

Zhichao Yin, Capital University of Economics and Business

Susan Sunila Sharma, Deakin University

This special issue examines how three interconnected forces—digital finance, demographic shifts, and behavioral decision-making—are transforming household financial behavior. Digital finance technologies are lowering barriers to entry and enabling personalized services, while demographic changes such as aging populations and evolving family structures are reshaping household risk management. Understanding how households make financial decisions remains critical to comprehending financial markets and macroeconomic dynamics.

The issue welcomes research using high-quality micro-level datasets to investigate how household-level financial choices aggregate into market-wide and macroeconomic effects. Contributions should address the complexity and heterogeneity of household financial decision-making across consumption, investment, borrowing, and wealth management activities, drawing insights from economics, finance, behavioral science, and data science.
